subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed away the observation that the two Drow had decided they weren't worth the effort.
source_quote: The two of them hadn't lowered their weapons so much as they'd decided we weren't worth the effort. I filed that away.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz appreciated that Nym used the past tense when referring to his concern for his safety.
source_quote: I appreciated the past tense. It did a lot of work.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that the fact someone hired professionals rather than acting directly was the most interesting part of the situation.
source_quote: That last part was the interesting part.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz had been running a list in the back of his head since Velkynvelve of entities that wanted him dead.
source_quote: I'd been running a list in the back of my head since Velkynvelve — the kind of list you keep when your life depends on knowing who wants what.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized that until this moment, the list of entities wanting him alive and protected had been empty.
source_quote: Entities with motive to see me alive and sufficiently protected to require hired blades from Menzoberranzan — that list had, until approximately this moment, been empty.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that asking the obvious question was important because the answer was rarely the obvious answer.
source_quote: You always ask the obvious question, because the answer is rarely the obvious answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately found Nym's elegant indifference toward Asha reassuring.
source_quote: Nym dismissed it with a kind of elegant indifference that I found, privately, somewhat reassuring.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that a third 'bravo' is never sincere.
source_quote: Three *bravos*. I have found, as a general principle, that a third *bravo* is never sincere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought that Kaelira’s puzzlement was genuine and not theatrical.
source_quote: And then she looked at me, and there was genuine puzzlement in it — not contempt, not theater. Actual, professional confusion at an anomaly that didn't fit the pattern she'd been given.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considered himself a nobody — with no house, no lineage, no claim to Drow societal currency.
source_quote: I had no house. No lineage with the right names. No claim on any of the structures that give a Drow life its currency in Menzoberranzan.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that someone in Menzoberranzan had paid a lot to keep him alive, and that the anonymity implied the payer had something to hide.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing: the payer has significant reason not to be associated with the purchase.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately thought that the entire chain of events might have started because someone decided to be friends with the wrong drow.
source_quote: The thought had a particular shape. Elegant, in the way that retrospective clarity sometimes is. The whole of it — the capture, the escape, Velkynvelve, the months of running — threading back to a single point. Me. A nobody. A nobody that someone in Menzoberranzan had interrupted their schedule over, more than once.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt he was standing at the edge of the question that changes everything, as described by Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel, that relentlessly hopeful halfling whose book I'd read too many times to admit, had a phrase for the sensation I was experiencing. He called it *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz admitted he literally had no idea why there was so much focus on him.
source_quote: I said what I actually believed, which is a thing I do less often than I probably should: 'I literally have no idea why there's all this focus on me.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir went very still when Asha Vandree declared herself in charge.
source_quote: The moment Asha Vandree declared herself in charge, something in me went very still.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought Asha's confidence was the problem because she had already decided she'd won.
source_quote: She said it with the absolute confidence of someone who had just survived something she shouldn't have — chaos, screaming, close calls that she'd already reframed as divine favor — and that confidence was the problem. *Excellent! Now that I am in charge!* ... Asha had already decided.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a saying from the Garden Shadow about the most dangerous person being the one who has already decided they've won.
source_quote: I've read rooms like this before. The Garden Shadow had a saying — or possibly Brother Quellin did, the one with the dusty robes who taught something about pressure points of social authority ... that the most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembered a class on decisive action under moral uncertainty taught by Brother Harren, though he didn't recall what was said.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Decisive action under moral uncertainty — the ethics of necessary violence, or something like that. I think it was Brother Harren, the one who never sat down, who taught it. I don't remember what he said. I remember it went on for a long time.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir made the decision to kill Asha Vandree because he believed someone had to make the call.
source_quote: I'm making a call," I said. ... I just happened to also be true. Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not look at Asha's body after killing her.
source_quote: I didn't look at the body.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin tried to retain the Drow sisters and asked what it would cost.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, tried to retain them. He asked what it would cost.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to kill Asha Vandree without necessity, stating he didn't like killing people if he didn't have to.
source_quote: I don't like killing people if I don't have to," Thorin said. "I mean, you know...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was probably filing away a theological observation about mysterious dispensations.
source_quote: Grygum was probably filing away some theological observation about mysterious dispensations.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum looked thoughtful when Daz suggested auditing the books of the mysterious payer.
source_quote: No one laughed. Grygum looked thoughtful, which is his equivalent.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed that Thorin's reluctance, Nym and Kaelira's calculation, Grygum's preference for alternatives, and Daz's neutrality were all reasonable and true.
source_quote: All of it was reasonable. All of it was true. I just happened to also be true.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt the particular weight of irony settle in his chest when holding the jailer's keys.
source_quote: I turned them over in my hands and felt the particular weight of irony settle in my chest.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the keys would have been very useful at the very beginning.
source_quote: You know, they would have been very useful in the very beginning,

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suspected the wax pouch was the more interesting item after taking it from Asha Vandree's body.
source_quote: I had the wax pouch, and I suspected it was the more interesting item.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was very tired immediately after reading the contents of the wax pouch.
source_quote: I was right. I was also, immediately, very tired.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the theological text in the wax pouch was tedious and boring (being diplomatic).
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration... It's very tedious and boring.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wondered whether the theological text was pre-craziness or post-craziness.
source_quote: Is this pre-craziness or post-craziness, do you think?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled seeing similar handwriting in a merchant who had been Tongued by a bardic curse.
source_quote: I had seen something like this before, in a completely different context — a merchant I once knew who had been Tongued by a bardic curse...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the ambiguity of whether Ilvara knew she wasn't resisting her corruption was the most troubling part.
source_quote: That ambiguity was the most troubling part.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought of Stroud sitting across from Protanther and realized even long preparation can leave blind spots.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the thing that undoes you isn't the opponent you've been studying — it's the thing you didn't know to look for.
source_quote: Sometimes the thing that undoes you isn't the opponent you've been studying — it's the thing you didn't know to look for.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum intended to examine Ilvara's prayer book gingerly because it was dangerous.
source_quote: I'll examine it gingerly.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that the prayer book told him things he did not want to know.
source_quote: It told me things I did not want to know.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that the marginalia in Ilvara's prayer book were in a different hand, indicating a second mind at work.
source_quote: A different hand. That detail mattered to me more than any of the specific words.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feared that Ilvara had written the marginalia herself in a state so altered her handwriting had changed.
source_quote: Or — and this was the reading that settled in my stomach like cold stone — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Ilvara had not resisted the corruption documented in her prayer book.
source_quote: She had not resisted it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the Living Serpent Head Scourge was a great museum piece.
source_quote: The Living Serpent Head Scourge sounds... It sounds like a great museum piece.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed acknowledging the craft of terrible objects is not the same as endorsing what they served.
source_quote: There is a tradition... of displaying items that are terrible in origin and remarkable in craft, on the theory that acknowledging the craft is not the same as endorsing what the craft served.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted his tooth back after Grygum mentioned it.
source_quote: Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt recognition and then something quieter beneath it when Grygum mentioned his tooth.
source_quote: Thorin looked up. Something shifted in his face — recognition, and then something quieter beneath it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz meant seriously when he said, 'We've come a long way.'
source_quote: He said it lightly. He meant it seriously.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir took the Drow cloak from Asha Vandree's body, and Grygum did not begrudge him that.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing... and I did not begrudge him that.

subject: Ilvara's corruption
fact: Ilvara's corruption timeline was legible in the marginalia of her prayer book, showing a gradual shift from normal devotion to altered thinking.
source_quote: The corruption timeline was legible if you knew how to read it. Ilvara had been normal... and then something had found the edge of her and started pulling.

subject: Asha Vandree's transformation
fact: Asha Vandree had become indistinguishable from the rot she served, justifying Grygum's efficient looting of her body.
source_quote: Asha Vandree had been a cleric of Lolth who had also become... indistinguishable from the rot she served.

subject: House Mizzrym's concern
fact: House Mizzrym's sealed orders revealed frantic concern over Ilvara's disappearance, unaware of her corruption.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you?

subject: Neverlight Grove's missed meeting
fact: The letter from Neverlight Grove confirmed Ilvara's political alliance had dissolved because she was lost to Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin decided the necromantic pearl was necromantic, based on its sensation, like the smell from a giant's larder.
source_quote: I decided, necromantic, the same way you decide the smell coming from the back of a giant's larder means something died in there a while ago.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intended to take the necromantic pearl because he would not leave anything useful in the cavern.
source_quote: I didn't need a name for it. It was worth something to the right buyer, and I was not going to leave anything useful in this cavern, so I pocketed it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt the bundle of ritual items was not equipment but evidence of Ilvara's madness.
source_quote: It wasn't equipment. It was evidence. It was Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to pray over the dead soldiers of House Mizzrym because he had nothing to say to them.
source_quote: I didn't pray over them. They'd come here doing what they were told by someone who had already lost her mind, and I had nothing to say to them that wasn't just 'better luck in another life.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realized the signet ring and documents proved House T'sarran had contracted to extract Daz alive.
source_quote: The documents were worse. What was left of them... confirmed what we'd been trying to piece together since the mage had arrived with her mercenary escort. There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considered Daz’s response to Nym’s skepticism to be the most restrained thing he could have said.
source_quote: Daz looked at her with something behind his eyes that I couldn't quite read. He let a beat pass, and then he said: 'So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?' Which was, I thought, the most restrained thing he could possibly have said in that moment.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin understood the necromantic pearl was not in the wrong place by accident — someone had placed it there.
source_quote: The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident. Someone had put something like it there, or something like it had grown there because the conditions were exactly right for it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembered Ilvara taking his tooth at Velkynvelve as a trophy and a symbol of power.
source_quote: When we'd first found ourselves hanging in nets at Velkynvelve, Ilvara had made a point of collecting trophies. It was the kind of thing a person does when they want their captives to understand the power relation clearly — she'd taken my tooth.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt the debt of his stolen tooth was now settled because he had recovered it.
source_quote: It was settled now. I had the tooth back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intended to keep silent about the significance of the tooth and the pearl because speaking would add nothing to the next ten seconds.
source_quote: I didn't say any of that out loud. Thorin Giantfriend, radical transparency, except when the thing being said wouldn't add anything to the next ten seconds.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wondered why powerful Drow houses would spend so much to extract him, given his lack of consequence.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence. I am a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan... My lineage is not distinguished. My House, if I ever truly had one, is not significant. I do not possess anything worth this level of orchestrated attention.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately catalogued the possibility of noble blood as embarrassing and preferred a more interesting answer.
source_quote: I have, privately, catalogued that possibility and found it embarrassing. Whatever the answer to this question turns out to be, I prefer it to be something more interesting than inherited blood I didn't earn.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz resolved to investigate his origins together with the party and split any proceeds from the discovery.
source_quote: I think,' I said, keeping my voice very even, 'that we should investigate this together. Whatever we find — whoever is behind this, whatever they think I'm worth — we split the proceeds.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Nym and Kaelira regarded him with skepticism that was precise, not cruel.
source_quote: Nym and Kaelira regarded me with the specific expression that Drow reserve for people they find simultaneously interesting and beneath consideration. The tone was sardonic in the way that only people trained in the same school of thought as me can manage — not cruel, just precise.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz accepted that the Duskryn sisters were not entirely wrong to be skeptical of his possible noble lineage.
source_quote: The uncomfortable truth is that they were not entirely wrong to be skeptical.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed the question of his identity away to return to it at inconvenient moments.
source_quote: I filed the question where I file most things that don't have immediate answers — in the part of my mind that I return to at inconvenient moments — and let the conversation move on.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that Dawnbringer refused to be used as a religious symbol for purification.
source_quote: I'm not some kind of magical wizard thingy that purifies things. I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things. I will not be treated like a religious symbol to be used and waved over corrupt—

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Thorin’s use of the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard was an effective tool for negotiating with Dawnbringer.
source_quote: I noted the outburst, noted Thorin's expression — the particular patience of a man who has had this conversation before and expects to have it again — and watched.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized that Thorin and Dawnbringer’s exchange had the comfortable rhythm of repetition — they had been here before.
source_quote: They had been here before, the dwarf and his sword. They would be here again.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz acknowledged that he carried unresolved questions about his identity alongside the party’s other burdens.
source_quote: I had an unanswered question about my own identity sitting unresolved in my chest, a pair of Drow mercenaries who found me either fascinating or ridiculous, and a sunblade that had just been persuaded to participate in something it found philosophically objectionable.

subject: Daz's identity
fact: Daz intends to uncover the truth about why he was targeted, even if the answer is not noble blood.
source_quote: Whatever the answer to this question turns out to be, I prefer it to be something more interesting than inherited blood I didn't earn.

subject: The necromantic pearl
fact: Thorin suspects the pearl is a key to understanding Ilvara’s ritual corruption, but has not yet named its origin.
source_quote: The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident. Someone had put something like it there, or something like it had grown there because the conditions were exactly right for it. Either answer was a problem that needed a name.

subject: The stolen tooth
fact: Thorin carries the recovered tooth as a symbol of closure from his captivity at Velkynvelve.
source_quote: It was settled now. I had the tooth back.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir stopped counting steps because counting had started to feel like superstition, as if he were measuring distance against the possibility of failure.
source_quote: I had stopped counting the steps somewhere around the third hour of climbing — not because I lost track, but because counting had started to feel like superstition, like I was measuring the distance against the possibility of failure.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had been thinking about the Overbright intermittently for months, not with anticipation but like a theory he had not yet been able to test.
source_quote: I had been thinking about this moment, intermittently, for months. Not with anticipation exactly — anticipation implies you trust the thing to happen. More the way you might think about a theory you have not yet been able to test.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had stopped trusting that the Overbright would be real.
source_quote: I had stopped trusting it would be real.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt the sunlight was a kind of violence, not pain, but the body registering that something fundamental had changed.
source_quote: what I felt when it touched my face was a kind of violence, or close to it. Not pain. Just the body registering that something fundamental had changed, the same way a deep-water creature might register the pressure dropping.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in sunlight.
source_quote: I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a class on material impermanence taught by Brother Quellin or another monk with chalk dust on his robe.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Some form of material impermanence — I think it was Brother Quellin, or possibly the tall one whose name I never quite caught, the one who always had chalk dust on his robe. The transience of tools. The attachment to implements. Something about a bowl and an empty hand.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the monastery curriculum’s focus on non-combat topics had not worked itself out for him.
source_quote: It had not, in fact, worked itself out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Glabbagool peering out of the bag of holding with wide, present eyes, observing the surface world with attention.
source_quote: There is no other word for it. He peered. He had not been in sunlight before. None of us were entirely sure what Glabbagool's eyes were, from a structural standpoint, but they were wide and present and sweeping across the surface world with an attention that made my own response to the Overbright seem, by comparison, measured.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found Glabbagool’s curiosity toward the surface world admirable, though he would not say it out loud.
source_quote: I found that admirable in a way I was not going to say out loud.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted that Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere.
source_quote: Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspected Daz was already drafting a journal entry.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz’s call, framed as a group discussion but pulled by Daz’s analytical gravity.
source_quote: The decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz's call, framed as a group discussion but with Daz's particular analytical gravity already pulling it toward a conclusion before the conversation began.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had no opinion on sword whisperers but noted the category and moved on.
source_quote: I had no opinion on sword whisperers. I noted the category and moved on.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembered Thorin’s serious belief in the existence of a sword whisperer for Dawnbringer.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about, which meant he believed this person existed and should be found.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew Grygum had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read and would treat Candlekeep as both research and pilgrimage.
source_quote: Grygum was the only one among us who had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read, and Candlekeep was going to be, for him, something between research and pilgrimage. He would look up the lore of Bahamut. He would pick up pamphlets. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir agreed with the group’s decision to spend their gold on adventuring gear rather than business ventures.
source_quote: We agreed on the gear.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought, as he stood at the tunnel’s mouth, that they had made it — and now there was everything else.
source_quote: I stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at a sky that went farther than anything I had navigated in months, and I thought: this is where we were going. We had made it. Now there was everything else.
